title: Getting Started
subtitle: From your first ore to the endgame

entries.title: Mod Overview
entries.summary: What this mod is about, on one page

blocks.text: You're awake, Tenno. The Kuva has seeped into this land. Read this briefing before you move.

Your quarry is the boss {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master}. It is no stray beast: each hunter gets only one, with a name and a rank of its own, and while others can help you fight it, only your answer counts against it. Knocking it down is not enough, Tenno. Solve the puzzle that belongs to you alone first; only then does the hunt succeed. <hl>Kuva Lich</hl> is a combat and progression mod modeled on Warframe. You mine and farm your way toward the answer, and a successful hunt brings powerful weapons and upgrade cards.
These upgrade cards are called mods, and they are not picky: vanilla swords and bows, weapons from other mods, any weapon takes them.
How a Round Plays

items: Mine: break {item:kuvalich:requiem_ore} with a {lang:enchantment.kuvalich.requiem_destroyed} pickaxe to collect Requiem cards and materials.

Nemesis: while you have no Lich, a {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling} turns up near you every so often; finish it off and your Lich is born. Once its rage is full, it comes looking for you on its own.

items.text: Farm: once your Lich is born, {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}s come at you in squads; knock them down and execute them for decryption progress, which comes in three stages; each full stage reveals an answer card.
Farm: once your Lich is born, {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}s come at you in squads; kill them for decryption progress, which comes in three stages; each full stage reveals an answer card.

items: Set the cards: place three Requiem cards in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_gate} in the order you think is right.

items.text: Confront: its health has three segments and it goes down each time one empties; step in and execute it with {lang:key.kuvalich.mercy}, the 1st, 2nd and 3rd times checking the first 1, 2 and 3 cards. Right all three times means decryption succeeds; a wrong stab lets it break free and flee, your Lich rank rises by 1, and you try another order.

Confront: your card order is checked on the spot when you kill a {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master}. The right order means decryption succeeds; a wrong one raises your Lich rank by 1, and you try another order.

items: Upgrade: use the Kuva weapons, mods and materials you earn to consecrate gear, install mods and fuse weapons at the utility blocks.
Next round: after a success the answer is rolled again, your next Lich is born when you finish off another Kuva Larvling, and the Kuva weapons you get from then on are higher level.

blocks.text: The Tutorial Path
Don't skip ahead. From the next page on, this section is a full tutorial. Press “Next” at the end of each page and it covers every feature in the order you meet it in play.

rows: Enchant a pickaxe, mine Requiem Ore
Set the answer, confront the Lich
Rewards, your Kuva weapon, utility blocks

blocks.text: After the tutorial come three quick-reference pages, [[start/materials]], [[start/faq]] and “Numbers at a Glance”. The other sections cover each system in full, and every chapter links to them at the end.
Operator, the ship's archives are in order, down to the last comma. Ordis is most <x>hon-- IRRITATED--</x> honored to serve.
Many terms in this book come from Warframe, and you do not need to have played it. The tables below explain in one line what each term means here; click “More” for the full page.
Enemies & Decryption

rows: The boss, called the <t>Lich</t> for short. Each hunter gets one of their own, with a name and a rank; finish it with the right card order for a big reward
An unborn Lich that turns up while you have none; finish it and your Lich is born

cells: A common Kuva mob that comes at you in squads once your Lich is born, called the <t>Thrall</t> for short; knock it down and execute it for decryption progress
A common Kuva mob that comes at you in squads once your Lich is born, called the <t>Thrall</t> for short; kill it for decryption progress

rows: 8 kinds of cards; three of them in a fixed order make the answer you need to find
Points you gain from Thralls and from your own Lich; each full stage reveals one answer card
The block where you place your three answer cards

cells: When you execute a Lich, its stabs check your cards one position at a time; right through all three executions is a success, a wrong stab is a failure
When you kill a Lich with three cards set, the answer is checked; all three in the right order is a success, anything else a failure

rows: Starts at 1 and rises by 1 with every failure; it starts over after a successful decryption

cells: Liches, Thralls and Larvlings go down instead of dying; step in and press a key to execute them
Liches and Larvlings go down instead of dying; step in and press a key to execute them

rows: Your Lich's rage; when it is full, the Lich comes looking for you
The panel you open from the {lang:block.kuvalich.requiem_gate}: your Lich's name, rank, rage and your last 5 judgements

blocks.text: Gear & Mods

rows: Unique weapons, 13 kinds in all, that drop on a successful decryption. Each has a built-in element and takes mods right away
A Kuva weapon's strength; it sets attack, attack speed and passives
Swappable upgrade cards with a few bonuses each. Installing costs nothing and you can remove them any time
One bonus on a mod, such as “+120% {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.meleeDamage}”
A freshly dropped mod shows no stats; right-click it in your main hand to turn it into a specific mod
Mods come in five tiers: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Prime, Riven
The fourth tier: stronger versions of ordinary mods, dropped only on a successful decryption
The fifth tier. Fully random stats that you can reroll with Kuva
Use a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} to give an ordinary item a stat panel, so it can take mods
A consecrated item's four base stats: damage, crit chance, crit damage, status chance
Merge two Kuva weapons into one to raise the level and change the element

cells: The material for leveling up mods

rows: Mod workbenches: the Weapon Arsenal for weapons, the Warframe Arsenal for yourself
You yourself; Warframe mods are installed on you and always active

cells: Yellow hearts from Warframe mods; hits take them first, and they refill on their own

blocks.text: Combat

rows: Extra damage added to your attacks, such as {lang:kuvaweapon.type.fire} or {lang:kuvaweapon.type.ice}
A chance on hit to apply an element's status effect to the target
A chance to deal multiplied damage; above 100% chance, crits move up a tier
Extra damage against one type of mob, such as undead
Temporary bonuses that grow by one stack per kill

blocks.text: Materials & Blocks

rows: Mainly for rerolling Riven mods; also crafts the Weapon Arsenal
The material for consecrating; also crafts the Warframe Arsenal
Dropped only by Thralls; the main ingredient of the utility blocks
1 per successful decryption; required for the advanced blocks
Three-into-one block: 3 cards into 1, 3 mods into 1; it also dismantles mods
The core upgrade block: consecrating, fusion, Forma and Riven rerolls all happen here

cells: Permanently raise a TACZ gun's damage with a Lich Reliquary

blocks.text: The word “Lich” first meant an undead sorcerer who returns from death. Kuva Liches in the Origin System return the same way: execute a Kuva Larvling, Operator, and it rises again as a nemesis that belongs to you alone. Ordis has never cared for things that refuse to stay executed.

entries.title: Ch. 1 · Mining Requiem Ore
entries.summary: Enchant a pickaxe, mine your first ore

blocks.text: The Lich can wait. Solving your puzzle takes Requiem cards, and those lie buried underground.
Objective: get a pickaxe with {lang:enchantment.kuvalich.requiem_destroyed} and mine your first {item:kuvalich:requiem_ore}. Expect this to take time, Tenno.
Orders

items: Get the enchantment: this is the hard part. {lang:enchantment.kuvalich.requiem_destroyed} is Very Rare and only shows up near the top of the enchanting table. Librarian villagers may sell the book as well; apply it to your pickaxe at an anvil.
Pick a pickaxe: diamond or netherite mines fastest, and Fortune makes no difference. Don't use Silk Touch; with it the ore drops nothing.

items.text: Find the ore: search between Y {cfg:ore_gen.requiemOreMinHeight} and {cfg:ore_gen.requiemOreMaxHeight}. {item:kuvalich:requiem_ore} sits in stone and deepslate, thickest in the middle of that band, and never in the Nether or the End.

items: Dig: with the enchantment, a block breaks in about 0.5 s. Each block has a {cfg:kuva_lich.cardDropChanceWithEnchant|pctv} chance to pay out, and a payout drops everything in the table below at once.

blocks.text: Rewards

items: kuvalich:khra
kuvalich:jahu
kuvalich:fass
kuvalich:lohk
kuvalich:netra
kuvalich:vome
kuvalich:xata
kuvalich:ris
blocks.caption: The 8 Requiem cards

blocks.text: Don't pass up {item:kuvalich:experience_ore}. A stone pickaxe is enough; it drops experience and has a 50% chance of {item:kuvalich:endo}, which levels up mods in Ch. 5.
Don't pass up {item:kuvalich:experience_ore}. A stone pickaxe is enough, and it drops experience.

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① Without the enchantment the ore still breaks, but slowly: about <t>2.5</t> minutes per block with diamond, a payout chance of only <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.baseCardDropChance|pctv}</t>, and Fortune pushes it <w>lower</w>. ② The ore never drops itself as a block. Cards and materials come only from the payout roll; XP is separate, <t>50-100</t> for breaking it with a diamond pickaxe or better, times <g>{cfg:kuva_lich.expMultiplier|x}</g> with Requiem Destroyed.

entries.title: Ch. 2 · Thralls & Decryption
entries.summary: Wake your Lich, then reveal cards from Thralls

blocks.text: Tenno, every Lich Thrall you find, you finish. Leave them no room to breathe.

Objective: first finish off a {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling} so your Lich is born; then build decryption progress from the {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}s that come for you and reveal answer cards, collecting {item:kuvalich:requiem_gem}s on the way to build a {item:kuvalich:requiem_gate}.
The answer belongs to you alone, Tenno. Everyone has a puzzle of their own, and its answer is 3 Requiem cards in a fixed order. The more progress you build, the more answer cards you see.
Orders

items.text: Wait for a Larvling: while you have no Lich, a {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling} finds you every {cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingIntervalMinMinutes}-{cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingIntervalMaxMinutes} minutes online, with a notice reading “{lang:message.kuvalich.larvling.appeared}”. Knock it down: the weapon it reveals, level and element included, is the one your future Lich will carry. Step in and press the {lang:key.kuvalich.mercy} key to execute it, and your Lich is born. Don't hit it again once it's down, or it dissolves; see [[enemies/kuva_larvling]].

Wait for a Larvling: while you have no Lich, a {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling} finds you every {cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingIntervalMinMinutes}-{cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingIntervalMaxMinutes} minutes online, with a notice reading “{lang:message.kuvalich.larvling.appeared}”. Kill it yourself, and your Lich is born, carrying the weapon settled when it appeared; see [[enemies/kuva_larvling]].

Wait for Thralls: once your Lich is born, a small squad of {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}s charges at you from out of sight every {cfg:kuva_lich.thrallSquadIntervalMinSeconds}-{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallSquadIntervalMaxSeconds} s, so there's no need to hunt for them.

Down, then execute: a lethal blow knocks a Thrall down, and it waits up to {cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds} s. Get within {cfg:kuva_lich.mercyReach} blocks and look at it; when “{lang:kuvalich.mercy.prompt.thrall}” appears, press the {lang:key.kuvalich.mercy} key (default X). Only a finished execution gives {cfg:kuva_lich.minDecryptionProgress}-{cfg:kuva_lich.maxDecryptionProgress} decryption progress and drops.
Kill them yourself: each one gives {cfg:kuva_lich.minDecryptionProgress}-{cfg:kuva_lich.maxDecryptionProgress} decryption progress. The final blow must be yours; melee and arrows both count.

items: Watch progress: each time you gain progress, a Kuva crystal lights up near the top of the screen; its outline and the liquid inside rise together to show how far this stage has come. Under it reads “{lang:kuvalich.hud.murmur.label}”, and the three small diamonds beside that show how many cards are revealed. The exact points appear above your hotbar.
Build a Requiem Gate: craft it from {item:kuvalich:requiem_gem} ×5 and Obsidian ×4, recipe below. Right-click it to check your progress and revealed cards as well.
Fill three stages: reach {cfg:kuva_lich.firstStage}, {cfg:kuva_lich.secondStage} and {cfg:kuva_lich.thirdStage} points in turn; each stage reveals one answer card.

blocks.text: Rewards

items: Answer cards: revealed cards appear as symbols in the triangle in the middle of the Gate, and the three trade places now and then. Which spot a card sits in says nothing about the order.

{item:kuvalich:requiem_gem}: only Thralls drop it, at {cfg:kuva_lich.slaveRequiemGemBaseChance|pctv} plus {cfg:kuva_lich.slaveRequiemGemLootingBonus|pctv} per level of Looting on your main-hand weapon. The blocks later on take a lot of them.
Other drops: a chance of {item:kuvalich:kuva}, {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} and mods.

blocks.title: One revealed card is enough to try
blocks.text: The full answer is fixed the moment the first answer card is revealed. From then on, whenever your Lich comes for you, you can try as the next chapter shows; more revealed cards only make the guess easier.

blocks.title: Lich Profile
blocks.text: Once your Lich is born, Thralls carry its name over their heads, as “its name + Thrall”; anyone without a Lich still sees “{lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}”. Open the {item:kuvalich:requiem_gate} and click the small text in its bottom right or press <t>K</t> to reach the {lang:key.kuvalich.lich_archive}: its name, rank, rage and what it is doing right now are all in there.

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① A downed Thrall can only be executed by whoever brought it down. If you or your pet landed the lethal blow, it's yours; if another player or their pet landed it, it's theirs. Only when no player dealt the lethal blow (a fall, another mob) does it go to the last player who hit it in the 5 s before it fell. If nobody hit it in those 5 s, nobody can execute it; it fades when its time runs out and gives no progress and no drops. One that falls into the void just dies and gives nothing either. ② Requiem Gems only use Looting on the weapon in your main hand at the moment of the execution; Fortune does nothing.

blocks.title: Farm together
blocks.text: Farming with friends pays: when a Thrall falls, everyone with a Lich within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallProgressShareRange}</t> blocks gets the same decryption progress, so there's no need to fight over the last hit; drops and rage go only to whoever finished it.

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① A Thrall finished off by a pet, lava, burning, or elemental damage such as Toxin, Gas, Electricity or Blast gives no progress and no drops. ② Requiem Gems only use Looting on your main hand; Fortune does nothing, and a bow kill counts as Looting 0.

blocks.title: Once your Lich is born, watch what you pick up
blocks.text: From then on, every stack you pick up off the ground has a {cfg:kuva_lich.confiscationChance|pctv} chance to be confiscated whole by it, and you only get it back once you finish it. See [[requiem/confiscation]]. It calls this a tax. I call it theft.

{lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}s won't come for you. Once you have a Lich, decryption progress comes only from it: each failed decryption (an execution with fewer than three cards set counts as one) is worth <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.masterPotionMultiplier|x}</t> a Thrall's progress.

{lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}s won't come for you. Once you have a Lich, decryption progress comes only from it: each time you take it down with fewer than three cards set, or a decryption fails, it is worth <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.masterPotionMultiplier|x}</t> a Thrall's progress.

entries.title: Ch. 3 · Confronting the Lich
entries.summary: Set the answer, finish off your Lich

blocks.text: Bringing me to my knees is easy, friend. Keeping me down is beyond you.
Putting me down is easy, friend. Making it count is beyond you.

Objective: put three Requiem cards into the {item:kuvalich:requiem_gate} in the order you guess, wait for your {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} to come for you, then finish it with those cards in place. The right order means decryption succeeds. This time it comes looking for you, Tenno.
Orders

items: Get the three cards: you must actually own the three kinds in the answer. They drop at random from mining, or you can build a {item:kuvalich:requiem_recast} and turn any 3 cards into 1 random card. Building it uses up a Requiem Gate, so make another afterwards.
Set the cards: open the Gate and put the cards in the top three slots, which are positions 1, 2 and 3 from left to right. Closing the screen saves them.

Wait for it: about {cfg:kuva_lich.lichArrivalDelayMinSeconds}-{cfg:kuva_lich.lichArrivalDelayMaxSeconds} s after its rage fills, it sends a transmission first, then appears somewhere near you out of sight, and its boss bar shows up at the top of the screen.

items.text: Don't want to wait: a {item:kuvalich:requiem_ultimatum} calls it right away, with no need for rage and no regard for cooldown. It is not used up while you have no Lich, while yours is already on its way or nearby, or while you are in a dimension it can't reach or on Peaceful. Ultimatums only drop on a successful decryption, with a {cfg:kuva_lich.requiemUltimatumDropChance|pctv} chance.

Execute: a lethal blow doesn't kill it; it goes down for {cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds} s instead. Get within {cfg:kuva_lich.mercyReach} blocks and look at it; when “{lang:kuvalich.mercy.prompt.lich}” appears, press the {lang:key.kuvalich.mercy} key (default X). Anyone can land the lethal blow, but only you can execute it.
Kill it: your cards are checked the moment it dies. Anyone can land the final blow, but you must be within 64 blocks of it.

blocks.text: How It Is Judged

Its health has three segments and it goes down each time one empties, so you execute it three times: the 1st time is 1 stab checking position 1, the 2nd is 2 stabs checking the first two, and the 3rd is 3 stabs checking the whole answer. The three slots at the bottom of the screen light up stab by stab, and a wrong one turns red; an empty slot counts as wrong. Get the first two right and it breaks loose, standing up with its next segment full to fight on.

cells: Still judged stab by stab, and an empty slot counts as wrong: reaching the first empty slot is a decryption failure (with no cards at all, the very first stab is wrong), same as “3 cards, any mistake” below
Not an attempt; you only get decryption progress, and it will still come back later

rows: <g>Decryption succeeds</g>: it is finished for good, the rewards described in the next chapter drop, and the round resets

cells: Decryption fails: the wrong stab lets it break free and flee; Lich rank +1, cards lose no durability, and you still get progress
Decryption fails: Lich rank +1, cards lose no durability, and you still get progress; it will come back later
After <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds}</t> s the segment refills and it stands up to fight on; only after <t>3</t> unexecuted downs in a row does it flee, giving nothing; this is not a failure
Each Lich rank gained: Kuva enemies hitting you
+{cfg:kuva_lich.increaseDamage|pct}, only from Thralls and Liches; other damage is unaffected
Each Lich rank gained: you hitting Kuva enemies
-{cfg:kuva_lich.reducedDamage|pct}, capped at 99.9%; other targets are unaffected

blocks.text: Rage, Arrival and Departure

cells: From time online alone, rage goes from empty to full in <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichRageOnlineMinutes}</t> min

rows: Its rage is full, but you are in a dimension it can't reach, on Peaceful, or sleeping or riding
You move more than <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichLeashDistance}</t> blocks away, change dimension, log out or die

cells: If it trades no blows with you and no one hits it for <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichIdleDepartSeconds}</t> s, it leaves too
Rage drops to zero, and it won't come again for at least <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichCooldownMinutes}</t> min
Rage drops to zero; once it is full again, it comes back

blocks.text: Guessed Wrong? How to Retry

Every failure is intel. On a wrong stab, the chat tells you which stab it was: wrong on the first stab means position 1 is wrong; right on the first and wrong on the second means position 1 is right and position 2 is wrong, and so on. Your last 5 results are kept in the attempt records of the {lang:key.kuvalich.lich_archive}.

Every failure is intel. On a failure, the chat says so if position 1 was right, and adds a second line if positions 1 and 2 were both right. <w>No message means position 1 is wrong</w>. Your last 5 results are kept in the attempt records of the {lang:key.kuvalich.lich_archive}.

Once all three cards are revealed, try any order first. If position 1 is right, swap the last two; if it is wrong, move another card into position 1. This way you fail at most 3 times, and the 4th try always wins. Let it laugh, right up until your answer is in place.
Fighting It

items: Bring two or three kinds of damage: rotate melee, bow and spells. Keep hitting with one kind and it resists that kind more and more; the denser the hexagon shield flashing on its body, the more it has adapted.

items.text: Bows first: arrows deal ×1.25 damage to Kuva enemies, and a star of golden cracks bursts open where they hit; other projectiles and spells only deal ×0.75.

Check its personality and weaknesses first: each Lich's personality, weaknesses and resistances are fixed when it is born. Open the {lang:key.kuvalich.lich_archive} and read the personality under its name and the “{lang:kuvalich.archive.attr.weakness}” and “{lang:kuvalich.archive.attr.resistance}” rows: a jovial Lich is fragile but grows fiercer fast, so end it quickly; a logical one is tough and adapts fast, so keep switching damage types. Its weaknesses take ×1.25–1.40 damage, so hit it with what it fears.

items: Leave pets behind: every attack the Lich makes also hits other creatures within a few blocks, pets and teammates included.
Pick a safe arena: don't finish it near lava or the void; rewards drop where it falls.

items.text: Finish fast: in combat its damage grows by {cfg:kuva_lich.battleBoost|pct} every second, so the longer the fight, the harder it hits, and the brighter the Kuva veins on its body glow.

blocks.title: The execution key
blocks.text: The <t>{lang:key.kuvalich.mercy}</t> key defaults to <t>X</t>, as in Warframe. X also does other things in vanilla (Creative's “Load Hotbar Activator”) and in many mods, so Controls shows it in red, but they don't clash: X only counts as Mercy while an execution prompt is showing or you're mid-execution, and that press won't also trigger anything else on X. The rest of the time X does what it always did, so there's no need to rebind.

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① A Lich from a spawn egg or /summon is not yours: it never goes down, and killing it gives nothing, no judgement and no progress. ② In an execution an empty slot counts as wrong: taking a card out does not dodge the judgement, and an incomplete set is still a failed decryption.

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① A Lich from a spawn egg or /summon is not yours: it never goes down, and killing it gives nothing, no judgement and no progress. ② If you're unsure, take one card out first; with an empty slot, taking it down only adds progress and never counts as a failure.

entries.title: Ch. 4 · Rewards & Blocks
entries.summary: Rewards, your Kuva weapon, new blocks

blocks.text: A delivery, Operator! Every piece the Lich leaves behind, Ordis would <x>take the Lich along-- in PIECES-- into the hold--</x> ahem, will log and file.

Objective: collect your decryption rewards, get to know your first Kuva weapon, then use the {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary} to build a {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}. A round yields only one Lich Reliquary, Tenno; decide where it goes before you spend it.
Rewards

rows: 1, the very weapon the Lich carried (one of 13), at the level and element the Larvling revealed

cells: <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.requiemUltimatumDropChance|pctv}</t> chance for 1; keep it, and once your next Lich is born, right-click to summon it

rows: Back to your inventory; each card lasts 3 successes

blocks.text: Apart from the cards that return to your inventory, rewards <w>drop where the Lich fell</w>. Pick up every last one, and quickly.
Revealing Mods
Dropped mods are unrevealed and show no stats. Right-click one in your main hand and it turns into a specific mod at your feet; pick it up.
Reveal them now, while the round is fresh. Until your next Lich is born, nothing you pick up can be confiscated.
Your Kuva Weapon

rows: The number at the end of the line under the item name; it sets attack, attack speed and passive strength
One of 7 at random; element damage = weapon level %
Comes already consecrated, so it takes mods right away
Hover to see it; hold SHIFT, CTRL or ALT for different views

blocks.title: Levels keep rising, so keep old ones
blocks.text: A new character's weapon level range is <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.baseMinimumLevel}-{cfg:kuva_lich.baseMaximumLevel}</t>, and your first Kuva weapon rolls somewhere in there. Each later success raises the range until it hits its cap. Keep old weapons as fusion material (Ch. 9).
Building the Utility Blocks

The five utility blocks form a chain. {item:kuvalich:requiem_gate} leads to {item:kuvalich:requiem_recast}, then to {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}, and both Arsenals are built from a Requiem Forge. Except for the first, each one <w>consumes the block it is built from</w>. The last three also need a {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary}, which is why you can only build them now.

blocks.title: Spend your first Reliquary on the Forge
blocks.text: The full set of five blocks needs <t>5</t> Lich Reliquaries, and each success drops only 1. Build the Requiem Forge first; consecration and most upgrades happen there.

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① Each tier eats the one before it. Building an Arsenal uses up your Requiem Forge, so to keep both, build another Forge. ② Break utility blocks with a diamond pickaxe or better, or they vanish outright.

entries.title: Ch. 5 · Installing Mods
entries.summary: Reveal, install and level up mods

blocks.text: No single card carries this hunt, Tenno; they have to complete one another.
Objective: install mods on your Kuva weapon, and learn to level them up and deal with spares. Eight mod slots, and what goes in them is your call.

Mods are swappable upgrade cards, each with a few <t>stats</t> such as “+120% {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.meleeDamage}”. Installing costs nothing and they come out any time; if a build does not work, swap it.
How to Install

items: Right-click unrevealed mods in your main hand to reveal them first.
Open the {item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table} and put your Kuva weapon in the weapon slot at the bottom; the 8 mod slots above become usable.
Put a mod in an empty slot to install it and take it out to remove it; <g>nothing is consumed</g>. Shift + left-click in your inventory places it automatically.
Take the weapon out and the mods stay stored on it, working wherever you take it.

blocks.text: Won't Fit?

items: Only one of each mod; the normal and Prime versions count as the same mod.
Different mods that boost the same stat may also conflict. When you pick up a mod, conflicting slots flash red.
At most 1 Riven mod per item.
Weapon mods and Warframe mods don't fit in each other's Arsenal.

blocks.text: Rarity and Sources

rows: Random drops from Requiem Ore and Kuva Thralls

blocks.text: Of the mods that drop, <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleWeaponRatio|pctv}</t> are weapon mods and the rest are Warframe mods (Ch. 7).
Leveling Up Mods
Mods have levels, and effect = max-level value × level ÷ <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel}</t>. A freshly revealed mod is usually level 1, only 1/{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel} of its full value.

items: Open the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}, put a mod in the left slot and {item:kuvalich:endo} in the middle slot.
The mod appears one level higher in the right slot; <g>the Endo is only spent when you take it</g>.
One level at a time; put the new mod back in the left slot to keep going.

rows: Put a single mod in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_recast}

blocks.text: Mods have no levels; every mod works at full strength as soon as you get it.
Spare Mods

items: Three-into-one: put 3 Bronze, Silver or Gold weapon mods of the same rarity in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_recast} to get 1 unrevealed mod of that rarity.

items.text: Warframe mods work the same way, but can't be mixed with weapon mods.
Dismantle: put in a single mod to turn it into {item:kuvalich:endo}. Higher rarity and level give more.

blocks.text: Press <t>Tab</t> in either Arsenal to open the mod Codex, which lists every mod except Rivens at max level.
Mods only work while a consecrated item is in your main hand. Kuva weapons come consecrated; for how to consecrate other weapons, see the next chapter.

blocks.title: Don't fill up on level 1 mods
blocks.text: A level 1 mod gives only 1/{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel} of its full value. Don't fill all eight slots with level 1 mods; spend Endo raising two or three key mods first.

blocks.title: Further records
blocks.text: [[modules/module_overview]] · [[modules/module_rarity]] · [[modules/module_level]] · [[weapons/requiem_recast]] · [[modules/module_codex]]
Origins do not decide how far a blade or bow will go. The hand that holds it does.
Objective: consecrate a vanilla or modded weapon so it can take mods too, and reroll its panel with {item:kuvalich:forma} if you don't like it. Settle on the weapon you mean to keep, then begin.
Consecrating

items: Open the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}. Put a single sword, axe, bow, crossbow or similar item in the left slot and a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} in the middle slot.
1 Sliver is spent at once and the consecrated item appears in the right slot, now with a random stat <t>panel</t>.
Take it to the {item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table} and install mods the same way as on a Kuva weapon.

blocks.text: The panel has four stats, {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.damage}, {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.criticalStrikeProbability}, {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.criticalStrikeMultiplier} and {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.triggerChance}. {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.damage} below 100% counts squared, so 80% is really 64%.

header: Share of its mods lent to your main hand

blocks.text: Forma: Rerolling the Panel

items: Craft {item:kuvalich:forma}, 3 at a time; recipe below.
In the Requiem Forge, put a consecrated non-Kuva weapon in the left slot and a Forma in the middle slot.
1 Forma is spent at once and the rerolled weapon appears in the right slot, its installed mods untouched. Reroll again if you don't like it.

blocks.title: Rerolling can lock the weapon
blocks.text: Decide where you will stop before you start. Each reroll has a {cfg:kuva_lich.formaLockChance|pctv} chance to lock the weapon for good. Normal Forma can no longer reroll it, and only {item:kuvalich:shadow_forma} from the Creative inventory can undo that.

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① A Kuva weapon's panel is fixed; Forma and Riven Slivers do nothing to it. ② An item can't be consecrated twice, so to change its panel, use Forma.

Operator, according to the records, Forma changes the polarity of a mod slot on a piece of equipment, at the cost of resetting that equipment's rank to 0 and starting it over. Here the name was borrowed for a panel reroll.

blocks.title: Further records
blocks.text: [[weapons/requiem_evolve]] · [[weapons/forma]]
Tenno, your strength answers to no one but you.

Objective: build a {item:kuvalich:requiem_warframe_table} and install Warframe mods on yourself. They are always active; you don't need to hold anything or wear armor. These mods live on you, and death can't take them.
Here the “Warframe” is you yourself, Tenno. Warframe mods and weapon mods don't fit in each other's Arsenal, so check which one is in front of you before you place them.
Orders

items: Build the Warframe Arsenal from {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}, {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} ×4, {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary} and Obsidian ×3. <w>It uses up a Requiem Forge</w>.
Right-click it; the 8 slots in the top two rows are your Warframe mod slots.
A mod works the moment you put it in and stops the moment you take it out.

blocks.text: Warframe mods come from the same places as weapon mods; of the mods dropped by ore, Thralls and Liches, <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleWeaponRatio|mul:-1|add:100|pctv}</t> are Warframe mods.
Rewards

items: Permanent bonuses such as health, armor, movement speed, resistances and mining speed. Identical stats across the eight mods mostly add up directly.
The mods are stored on you: any Warframe Arsenal shows your own set, and you don't lose them on death.

items.text: Shields: stacking {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.shield} gives you yellow hearts that take hits first. After you take or deal damage, they start refilling in about 10 seconds, as long as they aren't empty.

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.armor} multiplies the armor you already have, so with no armor on, any percentage still gives 0. ② {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.health}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.armor}, {lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.sprintSpeed} and a few others round down in 10% steps, so +25% really gives +20%.

In the Origin System, a Warframe is a biomechanical combat suit controlled by a Tenno. Ordis has always rather admired the workmanship. Warframes and weapons each have their own mod slots. Here, the “Warframe” is you yourself, Operator.

blocks.title: Further records
blocks.text: [[warframe/warframe_table]] · [[warframe/warframe_module]] · [[warframe/shield]] · [[reference/warframe_attr_survival]]
The moment you stop, what you have built starts draining away.

Objective: understand the most common kinds of mod stats, which are crits, elements, kill stacks and bane, so you know what to stack on your weapon. Learn how each kind counts before you pile it on, Tenno.
Weapon mod effects only apply while a <t>consecrated</t> weapon is in your main hand; unconsecrated weapons work like vanilla.
Crits

items: Crit chance above 100% isn't wasted. It upgrades the crit tier from yellow ×M to orange ×2M to red ×3M, where M is the crit multiplier.
Beyond 300%, more chance gives no extra benefit.
Fully charge your melee swings. An uncharged swing scales crit chance down with the charge, and damage drops even harder; a half-charged swing deals only about a fifth of a full-charge hit.
Crits only multiply the physical part; elemental damage never crits.

blocks.text: Elements

items: Element stats add elemental damage to every hit; when they <t>trigger</t>, they also apply that element's status effect to the target.

Two basic elements combine into a compound one, such as {lang:kuvaweapon.type.fire} + {lang:kuvaweapon.type.poison} = {lang:kuvaweapon.type.gas}. Which ones pair up depends on their order in the mod slots.
Kuva weapons have a built-in element; ordinary weapons rely on element mods.

blocks.text: Kill Stacks

Stats marked “Gained on kill” add 1 stack per kill. Without new kills they lose one stack at a time, every <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.weaponStackDecayTicks|sec}</t> for weapons and every <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.warframeStackDecayTicks|sec}</t> for Warframe mods. Stacks from Warframe mods work with any weapon, consecrated or not.
Bane
Bane stats make you hit one type of mob harder, and are often called “discrimination”. Thralls and Liches are both <t>undead</t>; against them, stack {lang:item.module.bane_of_undead}.

blocks.title: Damage numbers
blocks.text: The numbers that pop up on a hit show the health actually lost. White means no crit, and <c:F8FA2E>yellow</c>, <c:E8833A>orange</c> and <c:E6131E>red</c> are the three crit tiers. See [[combat/damage_numbers]].

blocks.title: Two traps
blocks.text: ① If the weapon itself has no element at all, no status chance will ever trigger. ② Mobs finished off by elemental damage over time, Electricity or Blast don't count as your kills and add no stacks.

Firearms aboard. Ordis has opened a new column in the armory accounts, down to the grade of polishing oil.

Objective: consecrate TACZ guns and install mods on them. With a spare {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary}, you can also upgrade a gun permanently. Guns don't follow quite the same rules as blades, so leave your blade habits behind.
Objective: consecrate TACZ guns and install mods on them. Guns don't follow quite the same rules as blades, so leave your blade habits behind.
Orders

items: In the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}, put a single gun in the left slot and a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} in the middle slot to get a consecrated gun.
Put it in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table} and install up to 8 mods.
Fire with the gun in your main hand; the mods apply straight away.

blocks.text: Which Stats Work on Guns

items: <g>Work</g>: ranged damage, ranged crits, elements, status, bane, kill stacks, plus a set of gun-only stats.
Don't work when shooting: melee stats, since a bullet hit is not melee.

blocks.text: Lich Enhancement: Permanent Upgrades

items: Put the gun in the Forge's left slot and a {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary} in the middle; 1 is spent, and the gun's base damage rises by <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.taczGunEnhancePercent|round:4|pct}</t> for good.
No consecration needed; any TACZ gun can be upgraded. Put the gun back in the left slot to upgrade again.

items.text: Each gun can be upgraded at most <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.taczGunEnhanceMaxCount}</t> times.

blocks.text: Consecrate first, then fire. An unconsecrated gun gets no mod effects at all, not even from mods on your offhand or armor.

entries.title: Ch. 9 · Loops & Endgame
entries.summary: Grow every round: levels, fusion, Rivens

blocks.text: One falls, another follows, Tenno. The Queens are never short of us.

Objective: see what to chase after each round, such as higher-level Kuva weapons, weapon fusion and Riven mods with good stats. Don't rush to throw away old weapons or old cards, Tenno; you will need them later.
What Changes Each Round

items: A success ends this Lich for good and resets your decryption progress, the answer and your Lich rank. The next round's answer is rolled again, and a new Lich is born when you finish off the next {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling}.

Both ends of your weapon level range rise by the same random amount, <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.minimumLevelCapIncrease}</t>-<t>{cfg:kuva_lich.maximumLevelCapIncrease}</t> levels, so later Kuva weapons are stronger.
The range has caps, with the minimum topping out at <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.minimumLevel}</t> and the maximum at <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.maximumLevel}</t>; beyond that, only fusion helps.
Each Requiem card lasts 3 successes. Old cards go into the {item:kuvalich:requiem_recast}, 3 for 1 new card.

blocks.text: Fusing Kuva Weapons

items: In the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}, put your main weapon in the left slot and another Kuva weapon in the middle; the two can be different kinds.
Take the result from the right slot, and the two become one.

blocks.text: New level = round down[ higher of the two levels × {cfg:kuva_lich.upgradeMultiplier|add:1} ], max {cfg:kuva_lich.upgradeLimit}

items: The result keeps the left weapon's type, panel and mods.
<w>Its element becomes the middle weapon's</w>. To give your main weapon a new element, put a weapon with that element in the middle.
The middle weapon disappears along with its mods, so take good mods off first.

blocks.text: Riven Mods: Rerolling Stats

items: Put a revealed Riven mod in the Forge's left slot and enough {item:kuvalich:kuva} in the middle. The card shows how many this cycle costs.

A card with new stats appears in the right slot at once, and <w>this is when you pay for this cycle</w>. Every preview costs Kuva, so changing the amount in the middle slot afterwards previews again and charges again.
Take it if you want the new stats, or take the original back to keep the old ones. Kuva already paid is not refunded, so every reroll has a price.

blocks.text: The ship's archives say Riven mods carry fully random stats, which can be rerolled, or “cycled”, with Kuva again and again. The more disposition dots a weapon has, the less popular it is, and the stronger its Riven stats.
Other Ways to Get Stronger

items.text: Level your key mods to the max (Ch. 5).

items: Unique enchantments, {lang:enchantment.kuvalich.lethal} and {lang:enchantment.kuvalich.first_strike} for swords, {lang:enchantment.kuvalich.escort} and {lang:enchantment.kuvalich.death_resistance} for armor, {lang:enchantment.kuvalich.experience_collector} for tools.

items.text: The Warframe stat “{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.itemDropMultiplier}” gives more drops from mobs.
The Warframe stat “{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.oreDropMultiplier}” gives more drops from ores.

items: Kill an animal or monster with {item:kuvalich:machete} in your main hand and each drop stack becomes 1-3 times as large.

entries.title: Common Pitfalls
entries.summary: The mistakes new players make most

blocks.text: No need to learn these the hard way, Tenno. Each entry names the mistake first, then what is actually true.
Mining and Blocks

items: × Mining Requiem Ore without the enchantment: about 150 s per block with a diamond pickaxe, a payout chance of only {cfg:kuva_lich.baseCardDropChance|pctv}, and Fortune makes it lower still. With the enchantment, it's about 0.5 s per block at {cfg:kuva_lich.cardDropChanceWithEnchant|pctv}.
× Mining ores with Silk Touch: neither Requiem Ore nor Experience Ore drops anything, not even the block itself.
× Breaking utility blocks with an iron pickaxe: all five need a diamond pickaxe or better, or they vanish. The Requiem Gate, Recast and Forge are also very slow to mine without Requiem Destroyed.

blocks.text: Decryption and the Lich

items: × Thinking the Gate eats your cards: cards are only registered to you and can be taken back any time, from any Requiem Gate. Only a successful decryption costs each card 1 durability (3 in total); failures cost nothing.
× Taking the clue slots as the order: revealed answer cards land in random positions, so you have to test the order. A {item:kuvalich:requiem_riddle} tells you the right order directly.

× Searching the world for a Lich: Liches don't spawn in the wild. Yours is born when you finish off a {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling}, and once its rage fills up, it comes looking for you. For the times it won't come, see [[start/tut_3_lich]].

items.text: × Farming Liches from spawn eggs or commands: a Lich made that way belongs to no one, and killing it gives nothing: no card check, no progress, no drops.

× Thinking the fight ends when the Lich drops: its health has three segments, emptying one only brings it down, and you have to walk up and press the Mercy key (default X) to execute it, three times in all. Only you can execute it, though others can help knock it down. If you don't execute it within {cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds} s, it refills that segment and gets back up; only after 3 missed downs in a row does it escape, which gives nothing and doesn't count as a wrong guess.

× Thinking you must land the killing blow on the Lich: whoever lands it, the result is checked against your cards, but you must be in the same world and within 64 blocks; any farther and nothing counts.

× Thinking that taking a card out only earns progress: the execution checks your order stab by stab, an empty slot counts as wrong, and one wrong stab lets it escape, raising your Lich rank by 1. Treat an uncertain order as a probe: on a failure, chat tells you which stab was wrong.

× Killing the Lich with cards you're unsure of: while all three slots are full, every kill is checked, and a wrong guess raises your Lich rank by 1. If in doubt, take one card out, and a kill only adds progress.

× Thinking a downed Thrall counts: a fatal blow brings Thralls down too, and only executing them gives decryption progress and drops. If no one executes it within {cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds} s, it fades away and gives nothing. Thralls downed by your pets or summons are yours to execute; one downed by other mobs, fire or lava can't be executed by anyone unless a player hit it recently.
× Letting pets or summons clear Thralls: Thrall progress and drops only count kills you make yourself; arrows you shoot count.

× Hitting a downed Larvling: once a {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling} is down, one more hit from anyone makes it dissolve on the spot, giving nothing, and the next one is a full wait away. Once it's down, stop attacking and go execute it.

× Thinking the X key is broken because it shows red in Controls: Mercy defaults to X, which vanilla Creative's “Load Hotbar Activator” and some mods also use, hence the red. It still works: X only counts as Mercy while an execution prompt is showing; the rest of the time it does what it always did.

items: × Expecting this round's answer to carry over: every success wipes progress and the answer and puts your Lich rank back to 1; the next round is rolled fresh, with a new Lich coming for you.

× Spamming one attack on the Lich: each hit of the same damage type gives it +5% resistance, up to 30%. The more hits within 2 seconds, the less each does, down to 40%, and any part of a single hit above 15% of its max health is heavily reduced. Mix damage types; see [[enemies/lich_resistance]]. The Lich Profile key (default K) shows its weaknesses and resistances.

items.text: × Thinking the Lich rank is just a number: each rank it gains makes damage from Thralls and Liches +{cfg:kuva_lich.increaseDamage|pct}, so every failure makes them harder. Falls, ordinary mobs and other damage are unaffected, and it resets on a successful decryption.

× Thinking the Lich rank doesn't touch your damage: each rank it gains makes your damage to Thralls and Liches -{cfg:kuva_lich.reducedDamage|pct}, capped at 99.9%, and other targets are unaffected. It resets on a successful decryption.

× Leaving valuables on the ground: once your Lich is born, every stack you pick up has a {cfg:kuva_lich.confiscationChance|pctv} chance to be confiscated whole, up to {cfg:kuva_lich.maxConfiscatedItems} stacks, and it comes back only when you vanquish it. Mods you reveal drop at your feet first, so they can be taken too.

blocks.text: Gear and Mods

items: × Installing mods before consecrating: an ordinary weapon must first be consecrated with a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}. Kuva weapons come consecrated.
× Using Forma on a Kuva weapon: {item:kuvalich:forma} only works on consecrated non-Kuva weapons. Kuva weapons get stronger through fusion.
× Two Rivens on one item: each item takes only 1 Riven, and so does your Warframe mod loadout; mods of the same type, or ones that conflict, can't be installed together either.

items.text: × Expecting full value from offhand or armor mods: slots other than the main hand apply at their own percentage; see [[modules/multi_slot]].

items: × Farming Thralls with Fortune: mob drops use Looting on your main-hand weapon, and only the {item:kuvalich:requiem_gem} gets a Looting bonus.
× Throwing away early low-level Kuva weapons: they make good fusion material, but fusion takes the element of the material weapon, so check its element before putting it in the middle slot.

items.text: × Filling a weapon with level 1 mods: level 1 is only 1/{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel} of the full value. Spend {item:kuvalich:endo} raising two or three key mods first.
